identification.summary: DiceyF is the name Kaspersky uses for an APT cluster that has targeted online casinos and other victims in Southeast Asia, reportedly for years [S1]. Kaspersky's October 2022 write-up describes an intrusion at an online casino development studio in which the actor deployed a malware framework it named GamePlayerFramework [S1]. Secondary coverage describes GamePlayerFramework as a C# rewrite of the C++ PuppetLoader malware, with Tifa and Yuna branches (Yuna being the more complex), and with functions such as cookie and clipboard theft, keylogging, screenshots and virtual desktop sessions [S3][S4]. Kaspersky reports overlap with LuckyStar PlugX and with Earth Berberoka/GamblingPuppet activity documented by Trend Micro [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Secondary reporting says the activity dates to at least November 2021, when Kaspersky's investigation began and found PlugX loaders and other payloads delivered through an employee monitoring service and a security package deployment service [S3].
identification.notes: Kaspersky's full two-part report with IoCs and YARA is stated to be available only to private report subscribers; only part of the technical analysis is public [S1]. The Earth Berberoka link is an overlap reported by Kaspersky, not a statement that the clusters are identical [S1]. Trend Micro tracks Earth Berberoka (also GamblingPuppet) as its own cluster and lists PlugX, Gh0st RAT, PuppetLoader, Xnote and HelloBot among its tooling [S2]. Keep Kaspersky DiceyF and Trend Micro Earth Berberoka facts separate [S1][S2]. Microsoft has no mapped name in the record; none was found in sources.

attribution.confidence: Kaspersky says the motive is unclear and that it saw no evidence of immediate financial gain; it suggests possible espionage and IP theft [S1]. Secondary outlets report Kaspersky and Trend Micro findings as pointing to Chinese-speaking/Chinese-origin actors, but no source reviewed names a state sponsor [S4][S2].
attribution.basis: Overlap with Earth Berberoka, which Trend Micro attributes to Chinese-speaking actors based on tooling such as PlugX and Gh0st RAT [S2][S4]. No government attribution to DiceyF was found.

objectives: Kaspersky assessed the motives as unclear, possibly a mix of espionage and intellectual property theft rather than immediate financial gain [S1]. Targeting of a casino game development studio is consistent with interest in source code or development assets, but sources do not state this explicitly.

targeting.notes: Kaspersky reports DiceyF targeting online casinos and other victims in Southeast Asia, with a specific intrusion at an online casino development studio [S1]. Trend Micro's related Earth Berberoka reporting describes gambling sites, mainly in China, as targets [S2]. Specific victim names and countries were not given in the sources reviewed.

capabilities.summary: GamePlayerFramework is a modular framework that secondary reports describe as a C# variant of PuppetLoader, offered in Tifa and Yuna branches, with remote access, keylogging, clipboard and browser cookie theft, screenshots and virtual desktop sessions [S3][S4]. Kaspersky states the actor continuously evolved its codebase and added encryption [S1]. Secondary reporting says the actor delivered PlugX loaders and other payloads through an employee monitoring service and a security package deployment service, and used a fake employee data synchronization app lure that dropped Yuna downloaders inside the network [S3][S4]. Kaspersky's public text notes that lack of obfuscation in GamePlayerFramework eases YARA-based detection [S1].

campaigns.name: GamePlayerFramework at casino development studio
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky published its DiceyF analysis describing GamePlayerFramework deployed in an online casino development studio, with overlaps to LuckyStar PlugX and Earth Berberoka [S1]. Media coverage the same month repeated the espionage and IP-theft assessment [S3][S4].

diamond.adversary: Unnamed actor tracked by Kaspersky as DiceyF; overlaps with Earth Berberoka/GamblingPuppet and LuckyStar PlugX; Chinese-speaking/Chinese origin per secondary reporting; no sponsor named [S1][S4].
diamond.capability: GamePlayerFramework (Tifa and Yuna branches), PuppetLoader lineage, PlugX loaders [S1][S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Delivery through an employee monitoring service and a security package deployment service inside the victim environment [S3]. C2 details are in Kaspersky's subscriber report and were not reviewed.
diamond.victim: Online casinos and an online casino development studio in Southeast Asia [S1].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints; C# framework with encryption; internal software deployment and monitoring tools used as distribution channels [S1][S3].

gaps: Kaspersky's full two-part report, IoCs and YARA rules are subscriber-only and were not reviewed [S1].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Operational environment: online gambling and casino game development firms in Southeast Asia [S1]. Adversary: Chinese-speaking cluster with espionage/IP-theft interest overlapping Earth Berberoka [S1][S2]. MLCOA: continued framework updates with encryption and abuse of internal deployment and monitoring services to spread PlugX or GamePlayerFramework within development networks [S1][S3]. MDCOA: pivot to supply-chain style compromise of game or software products built by a compromised studio; this is an inference not stated in sources. Candidate indicators: PlugX loaders or Tifa/Yuna downloaders pushed via employee monitoring or package deployment tools; YARA hits on unobfuscated GamePlayerFramework [S1][S3].

provenance.importedSummary: DiceyF is an advanced persistent threat group that has been targeting online casinos and other victims in Southeast Asia for an extended period. They have exhibited overlapping activity with LuckyStar PlugX and Earth Berberoka/GamblingPuppet, as reported by various cybersecurity vendors. While their motivations remain unclear, previous incidents suggest a combination of espionage and intellectual property theft rather than immediate financial gain. DiceyF continuously evolves their codebase and adds encryption capabilities to enhance their stealthy cyberespionage activities.
